title: Right derived functors and coherent nonnegative total complexes
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], with ordinary derived categories and K-injective right derived functors [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a left exact additive functor [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let $\Delta$ be the small category of finite nonempty ordered sets $[n]=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and order-preserving maps, and let $K:\Delta\to\operatorname{Ch}^{\ge0}(\mathcal A)$ be a strict cosimplicial diagram of nonnegative cochain complexes. Write $K^{n,q}=K([n])^q$ and $\delta=\sum_{i=0}^{n+1}(-1)^i d^i$ for the alternating coface differential. Define $T(K)^r=\bigoplus_{n+q=r}K^{n,q}$ with differential $\delta+(-1)^n d_K$ [def-sp-double-complex-total], and write $Q$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms.
There are compatible nonnegative injective replacements of the complexes $K([n])$, retaining all cosimplicial operators, for which the resulting resolved total computes $RF(QT(K))$. In particular there is a canonical isomorphism in $D(\mathcal B)$
$$\chi_{F,K}:RF(QT(K))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{n\ge0}RF(QK([n])).$$
The right hand side means the total of this coherently resolved diagram, rather than a total assigned to a diagram only in the ordinary derived category. If a nonnegative resolution degree $s$ is added, only triples $n,q,s\ge0$ with $n+q+s=r$ contribute to total degree $r$. The comparison is induced by the right-derived comparison maps on these resolutions and the canonical finite-biproduct identifications.
It is independent of compatible resolution choices and natural in strict cosimplicial chain maps. For a strict augmentation $\operatorname{const}(A)\to K$ with $A$ a nonnegative complex, let $a:A\to T(K)$ have component $a^0$ in cosimplicial degree zero and zero in higher cosimplicial degrees. Then $\chi_{F,K}\circ RF(Qa)$ is the totalized derived augmentation $RF(QA)\to\operatorname{Tot}_{n\ge0}RF(QK([n]))$. These assertions include compatible maps of augmented diagrams. No preservation of injectives by an unrelated exact functor is assumed.

Agent extension to nonnegative cosimplicial complexes using injective resolutions in their small diagram category; the precise natural derived comparison, including augmentation, is stated here.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-functorial-injective-embedding], $\mathcal A$ has functorial injective embeddings. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-functorial-bounded-injective-resolution] to obtain one functor $I$ on bounded-below complexes and a natural quasi-isomorphism $\eta_C:C\to I(C)$, preserving every strict lower bound. Put $J_n=I(K([n]))$ and $u_n=\eta_{K([n])}$. For every $\theta:[n]\to[m]$, set $J(\theta)=I(K(\theta))$. Functoriality retains every cosimplicial identity, and naturality of $\eta$ says $J(\theta)u_n=u_mK(\theta)$. Thus $u:K\to J$ is a strict map of cosimplicial complexes. Every $J_n$ is nonnegative with injective terms. The same construction applies simultaneously to an augmented diagram, including its augmentation object.

proof.text: For $C=K,J$ form the first-quadrant double complex $D_C^{n,t}=C_n^t$ with first differential $\delta_C=\sum_i(-1)^i C(d^i)$ and second differential $d_C$. Paired cosimplicial identities cancel the summands of $\delta_C^2$; the cofaces are chain maps, so $d_C\delta_C=\delta_Cd_C$. Therefore [def-sp-double-complex-total] gives $T(C)$ with differential $\delta_C+(-1)^n d_C$. Naturality of $u$ makes $T(u):T(K)\to T(J)$ a chain map. For each fixed $n$, its internal-degree column map is the quasi-isomorphism $u_n$. That comparison asks for quasi-isomorphisms along the second index ($\mathrm{flip}.X\,n$), so apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison] to the transposed double complexes $D_C'^{t,n}=C_n^t$, with first differential $d_C$ and second differential $\delta_C$; its maps at fixed second index $n$ are the $u_n$. The maps $(-1)^{nt}$ on the summands $C_n^t$ give chain isomorphisms $\operatorname{Tot}(D_C')\cong T(C)$, natural in maps of double complexes: both differentials of $\operatorname{Tot}(D_C')$ on $C_n^t$, namely $d_C$ and $(-1)^t\delta_C$, become $(-1)^n d_C$ and $\delta_C$ after the sign. Hence $T(u)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Both indices are nonnegative, as required by that comparison.

source.place: Tag 0133, lemma-double-complex-gives-resolution and finite-diagonal comparison, applied to the map of first-quadrant complexes

proof.text: For $r\ge0$, $T(J)^r=\bigoplus_{n=0}^r J_n^{r-n}$, and it is zero for $r<0$. This finite biproduct is injective: a map from the source of a monomorphism into it is a finite tuple of maps to the injective summands; extend each component across the monomorphism and combine them by the biproduct universal property. Thus [lem-sp-kinjective-computes] (2) makes $T(J)$ K-injective; it also makes every $J_n$ K-injective. Together with the preceding quasi-isomorphisms these are injective models of $T(K)$ and $K_n$. If an additional nonnegative resolution index $s$ is used while retaining original degree $q$, total degree $r$ has $n+q+s=r$; there are only finitely many such triples. Its differential has signs $\delta+(-1)^n d_q+(-1)^{n+q}d_s$, exactly those obtained by first totaling $(q,s)$ and then $n$. No infinite product or coproduct comparison is needed.

proof.text: Let $\beta_J:F(T(J))\to T(FJ)$ be the degreewise finite-biproduct comparison. Its inverse is induced by the maps $F(\iota_{n,t})$ into $F(T(J)^r)$, where $\iota_{n,t}$ are the summand inclusions. The biproduct projection-inclusion identities prove that these maps are inverse. By [def-sp-left-exact-additive], $F$ preserves finite biproducts and addition, so $F(\delta_J)=\sum_i(-1)^iF(J(d^i))$ and $F((-1)^n d_J)=(-1)^nF(d_J)$. Checking each summand therefore proves that $\beta_J$ is a chain isomorphism. The same summand calculation proves $T(Fg)\beta_J=\beta_{J'}F(T(g))$ for every strict map $g:J\to J'$.

proof.text:
For a bounded-below injective complex $C$, write $\rho_C:RF(QC)\xrightarrow{\sim}QF(C)$ for the inverse of the right-derived unit on $C$. The specified-resolution comparison of [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality] gives the normalized isomorphisms $c_{u_n}=\rho_{J_n}RF(Qu_n):RF(QK_n)\to QF(J_n)$, compatible with every cosimplicial operator. Define the coherent total on the right of the statement to be $QT(FJ)$ with these column identifications. Define
$$\chi_{F,K}=Q(\beta_J)\,\rho_{T(J)}\,RF(QT(u)).$$
All three factors are isomorphisms by the preceding steps and [lem-sp-kinjective-computes]. This is an isomorphism of entire derived objects. Its normalization uses the given augmentation $T(u)$ and the inverse derived unit, rather than choices of isomorphisms on cohomology.

proof.text:
For a strict cosimplicial chain map $f:K\to L$, $g_n=I(f_n)$ gives a strict map $g:J_K\to J_L$ and $g u_K=u_L f$. Totalize this square. By [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality],
$$QF(T(g))\,c_{T(u_K)}=c_{T(u_L)}\,RF(QT(f)).$$
Compose with the chain-isomorphism naturality $QT(Fg)Q\beta_{J_K}=Q\beta_{J_L}QF(T(g))$ from step 4. This gives $QT(Fg)\chi_{F,K}=\chi_{F,L}RF(QT(f))$. Identities and composites are respected because the chain-level maps, $F$, $I$, $T$, and $RF$ respect them. Columnwise the same naturality statement identifies $QF(g_n)$ with $RF(Qf_n)$. Thus the totalized map is the coherent derived-image map specified in the statement.

proof.text:
To compare any two compatible nonnegative termwise injective replacements $v:K\to L$ and $w:K\to M$, apply the fixed resolution functor $I$ to obtain the strict zigzag
$$L\xrightarrow{\eta_L}I(L)\xleftarrow{I(v)}I(K)\xrightarrow{I(w)}I(M)\xleftarrow{\eta_M}M.$$
Every arrow is a columnwise quasi-isomorphism: this is true of $\eta$, and follows for $I(v),I(w)$ from $I(v)\eta_K=\eta_L v$ and its analogue by two-out-of-three. All columns are bounded below and termwise injective, so [lem-sp-kinjective-computes] (1) makes these column maps homotopy equivalences; additive $F$ preserves a homotopy inverse and its homotopies. Apply [lem-sc-first-quadrant-total-column-comparison] in $\mathcal B$, through the sign-$(-1)^{nt}$ transposition of step 2, to see that all arrows of the zigzag of $T(F(-))$ are quasi-isomorphisms. Naturality of $\eta$ makes each leg commute with its augmentation from $K$; after totalization, [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality] identifies each leg with the corresponding normalized comparison from $RF(QT(K))$. Hence this zigzag identifies the two displayed $\chi$ maps. Any other zigzag commuting with the augmentations has the same identification, since it must equal $\chi_M\chi_L^{-1}$. This proves independence and its compatibility with the naturality equation of step 6.

source.place: Tag 0141, lemma-functorial-injective-resolutions and remark-match; common functorial-resolution zigzag, with normalized comparison by the derived unit

proof.text:
Let $b:\operatorname{const}(A)\to K$ be the strict augmentation. Resolve the entire augmented diagram by $I$: its augmentation is $I(b):\operatorname{const}(I(A))\to J$, and $u_n b_n=I(b_n)\eta_A$. Define $b_J:I(A)\to T(J)$ by $I(b_0)$ into cosimplicial degree zero and zero in other cosimplicial degrees. The augmentation identities give $J(d^0)I(b_0)=J(d^1)I(b_0)$, so its coface differential is zero. It is therefore a chain map and $b_J\eta_A=T(u)a$. By [lem-sp-derived-injective-resolution-naturality] this square gives
$$QF(b_J)c_{\eta_A}=c_{T(u)}RF(Qa).$$
Under $\beta_J$, $F(b_J)$ is the map with $F(I(b_0))$ in cosimplicial degree zero and zero elsewhere, by its summand definition. This is exactly the totalized derived augmentation, since the column comparisons identify $F(I(b_n))$ with $RF(Qb_n)$. Therefore $\chi_{F,K}RF(Qa)$ equals that augmentation. For a map of augmented diagrams the equalities $f_n b_n=b'_n h$ remain equalities after $I$ and $F$; in degree zero they give the total augmentation square, and in higher cosimplicial degrees both augmentation components are zero. Steps 6 and 7 transport this square through all normalized comparisons and resolution changes.
